summary: Fundraiser by Uyghur Anthology : Support the Contemporary Uyghur Anthology This anthology funds Uyghur writers and artists, translation, events, and community growth Uyghur Anthology is organizing this fundraiser. The Contemporary Uyghur An
content:
Fundraiser by Uyghur Anthology : Support the Contemporary Uyghur Anthology
This anthology funds Uyghur writers and artists, translation, events, and community growth
Uyghur Anthology is organizing this fundraiser.
The Contemporary Uyghur Anthology is a publication that platforms Uyghur (and anyone drawing their roots from East Turkistan) artists and writers in the diaspora by providing a space that is often inaccessible to those in our community. There are no other projects of its kind in the English language, and with two volumes already published, we hope to take this project to the next level. It's a rare look at Uyghur expression in an environment where all our stories are told by people pushing their own narratives without the intimate knowledge of our lived experiences.
<"Manifesto" by Sumayah Jurad from Vol. II>
We asked ourselves these questions - why wait for others to invite us to the table when we can pull up a chair and introduce ourselves? Why let others speak for us without trying first to speak? Our broken English can only be improved with audacity, and world literature is only enriched by the presence of new voices.
All-in-all, our efforts have been met with support from our community and pleasant surprise from those who did not know what they did not know.
Somewhat unprecedented is that we publish the authors' original language alongside the translation. Our book is filled with Uyghur, Latin, Cyrillic, and Chinese script to encapsulate as much of our community's experience as we can.
There are many publications in diaspora communities that platform East and South Asians, SEA, MENA, and more. Central Asia is often underrepresented in world literature or Asia-specific publications, and occupied territories even less so. Uyghurs themselves have been a relatively new diaspora community in English-speaking countries, and haven't had the opportunities to grow their literary or artistic communities. Many don't have the tools to nurture their talents, or knowledge of creative networks or opportunities, even when many journals seek work from underrepresented groups. In instances where they are aware, it's difficult to be published in this competitive field without the education and styles that publications look for. There are only a handful of literary translators translating from Uyghur to English, and not many Uyghurs who have had the chances to develop their creative language when learning English.
To sum up, the issues were:
No spaces for Uyghur writers and artists to develop their skills
A disconnect from artist communities, be it local or online
No bridge between our native tongue and English, and in turn, world literature
So, we put together a small group at the Tarim Network to take on this challenge. Completely volunteer-run; the very essence of a passion project. We did a call-out for anything and all. New writers, established writers, any language, any genre, whatever we could print in a book. And here we were, the first book of its kind, created to speak for ourselves without outsider voices, without a publishing house, raw and straight from the source.
<From the launch of Vol. I at Harvard University>
"The Contemporary Uyghur Anthology is a collection of Uyghur reflections in diaspora. Weaving together memories of the homeland, experiences of displacement, and transitions of identities, this anthology is a creative reflection of the beauty and complexities of the Uyghur experience.
By centering Uyghur voices at the forefront, this anthology serves as a form of living memory in a pivotal moment of Uyghur history. The title Under the Mulberry Tree refers to a story from the Uyghur literary classic Ana Yurt, where youthful Nuri faces terrible injustices, separation, and turmoil; but for one moment in the Charbagh, his love for Sebihe and his own family is full, ripe, and sweet, like the mulberries from the ancient tree. In a similar way that the mulberry tree offered comforts in Nuri’s time of need, we hope this volume offers a place of reflection and celebration of Uyghur culture."
We'd partnered with a member from a Jewish organisation to run writing workshops and explain editorial processes, as we had never worked on something like this before. After that collaboration, we decided to publish a revised edition on our own. This time, we added editors' notes to the pages to explain certain terms and historical and cultural contexts - mainly for our own youth, who don't always have access to cultural education. We translated more pieces from Uyghur and Chinese. Our contributors spanned 13 countries, at all levels of experience.
Was this work sustainable? Equipped with the tools, experience, and outpouring of support from our first volume, we spent the next two years saying yes. Our first book was now in libraries, there were articles and academic papers that mentioned it, and most of all, we reaffirmed the need for this sort of work. Not only were we accepting submissions, we worked one-on-one with emerging writers and artists to edit their pieces. We also helped first-time translators have their first publications with help from more experienced translators, as well as connecting them with the original authors.
Our second volume was even better than the last. From the blurb:
"How do we respond to the unexpected, and how does it influence perceptions of ourselves or the environments in which we exist? As a diaspora population, unexpected encounters can shape and transform what it means to be Uyghur as we build a new life outside of the homeland. Encounters Under the Mulberry Tree takes on the literal, abstract, and expanded renditions of these moments. We feature contemporary and historical works, including art, poetry, and prose in five languages with contributors based in a dozen countries, from established writers like award-winning author and filmmaker Tahir Hamut Izgil, to emerging artists, writers and translators of all ages. This book is a library of vignettes that grapple with intersections and how we make sense of it all."
Five languages (Uyghur, English, Chinese, Russian, Turkish)
<Vol. II showcased at a college hosted by Rawan Mentorship>
Now we embark on our third volume. The three of us do this while maintaining full time jobs, academic careers, and other side projects. We all live in different countries and have only met in person once. But it's something that we need to do, for our community and for ourselves. Our contributors have gained so much from this experience and we want to extend this opportunity to more people. This needs to survive in order for similar initiatives to be born.
Supporting the editors - all expenses so far have been paid out-of-pocket or through book sales. We do not have any donors or sponsors (yet!).
Supporting our contributors - we cannot afford to pay any of our contributors. Despite this, we have given free copies of the book to contributors, but this is definitely leaving a dent in our pockets.
Recruiting more people - paid internships or remuneration for one-off work would help volunteers spend more time on this project in this economy.
Enhance our level of expertise - we want to improve. Workshops or courses for our editors and contributors, professional feedback, the works. Unfortunately there is no one who speaks Uyghur and who is involved in Western publishing or English literature on a professional or academic level. We would appreciate connections with professionals from any language background, or the funding to level up.
Expand our network - we'd love to promote our work at literary festivals, go to conferences, do book events, establish ourselves in the public eye, provide reader copies to reviewers, and so on. However, there is a funding barrier to overcome to be able to attend these events, organise, or pre-order books.
<Vol. I on display at the Mosquers Film Festival, 2025>
Munawwar Abdulla is an Uyghur advocate, poet, and scientist born on unceded Kaurna land (Australia) and based in Massachusetts. She co-founded The Tarim Network, runs Uyghur Collective, and collaborates on projects with Uyghur rights organisations around the world. Her writings and literary translations have been published in places such as Modern Poetry in Translation, Asymptote, the Margins, the Georgia Review, and others.
Sonya Imin is a mixed Uyghur American scholar and multi-disciplinary creative who has worked on art and film projects across the US, Europe, and Central Asia. Growing up between the borderlands of the Uyghur homeland, broader Central Asia, and the midwestern United States, interrogations of belonging, home, and displacement influence the nature of her work. Currently based in Brussels, she is working on her doctoral research on Uyghur artistic production in the diaspora.
Maidina Kadeer is a mixed Uyghur-Hui writer and editor, born in Ghulja and currently based in Montreal (Tiohtià:ke), Canada. She holds a BA in English Literature and Law and Society from Concordia University, with a focus on post- and neo-colonial literature. Her work explores Uyghur identity, history, and culture through cuisine, agriculture, and neo-colonialism. She has contributed to projects such as a poem, NinetySix, in Slavs and Tatars’ Contest of the Fruits (2021) and participates in panels and interviews on Agriculture and Food History to raise awareness about Uyghur culture.

Nurnisa Kurban for Uyghur Academic Foundation
Uyghur Cultural Preservation and Survival Through Education
The Uyghur people have been persecuted and subjected to repressive Chinese government policies in their Indigenous homeland of East Turkestan for many years. It is estimated that up to three million Uyghurs have been interned, imprisoned, and enslaved in detention centers, prisons, and forced labor facilities throughout China since 2017.
In 2021, the Uyghur Tribunal found that China was committing genocide and other crimes against humanity against Uyghurs. In 2022, the United Nations also concluded that China was committing human rights violations against Uyghurs amounting to crimes against humanity. Countries including the United States, Canada, the Netherlands, Czech Republic, United Kingdom, Lithuania, Belgium, and France have all declared a genocide in East Turkestan. Despite these declarations of genocide and related reports by various human rights organizations, atrocities against Uyghurs continue today with very limited international recognition and accountability.
During this time of ongoing genocide and cultural erasure in their Indigenous homeland, Uyghurs of the diaspora are working to preserve their culture and identity as a matter of survival. Uyghur education has been eradicated by the Chinese State, Uyghur texts are forbidden and in danger of being eliminated, and the Uyghur language itself is prohibited.
Uyghur scholars, linguists, and other specialists in the diaspora worldwide serve on the Uyghur Language and Education Committee of the Uyghur Academy to preserve the work of Uyghur intellectuals who have been persecuted and forcibly disappeared. This work has been ongoing since 2009 and is continuing to expand.
The Committee has created standards-aligned K-5 textbooks, which include classic and contemperory Uyghur literature, poetry, historical texts, and biographies for Uyghur children to learn about their own culture and identity in their native language. The Committee is seeking funding to expand and revise the existing K-5 textbooks, create teacher’s edition textbooks for educators, and design supplemental resources. They also hope to develop Middle and High School textbooks and related supplemental resources. To effectively implement these educational materials, they would also like to provide training for teachers.
Please consider supporting this urgent work of the Uyghur Academic Foundation as a matter of cultural survival for future generations of the Uyghur people.

Sarah Elder is organizing this fundraiser on behalf of Silkroad Uyghur.
In 2018, Gairatjan Rozi, a talented Uyghur chef, trained in Europe and now settled in America, opened 'Marco & Polo' in Hyattsville. The restaurant's menu features the cuisine of his homeland, in the Uyghur Autonomous Region of China, with classic Uyghur dishes including hand-pulled laghman noodles, dumplings, and lamb kebabs, complemented by more familiar Turkish and Mediterranean fare.
Within just a few years, Mr. Rozi and his restaurant has earned the love of our community. His food & restaurant has been featured in the local press and has earned a dedicated following in the Washington DC region.
Unfortunately the COVID-19 pandemic is forcing Mr. Rozi to close his family-run kitchen, shutter his beloved restaurant, and put in storage his colorful collection of Uyghur artifacts which decorate 'Marco & Polo.'
But Mr. Rozi is hopeful. Having dedicated his new life in America to 'Marco & Polo,' he dreams of reopening his restaurant soon - in a new location that will attract even more customers who want to enjoy & explore both the cuisine and the Uyghur culture of Central Asia.
Your generous donation to this GoFundMe effort will help Mr. Rozi begin to recover finically from the COVID-19 disaster and allow him to pursue his dream of creating another unique Uyghur dining experience for our community! Rehmet! (Uyghur for 'thank you')

content:
Fundraiser by David Xia : Fighting for legal fairness
David Xia and 2 others are organizing this fundraiser.
Supporting Yeliang Xia with donation for legal defence against the evil fugitive billionaire Wengui Guo (most wanted by Interpol)
Mr. Yeliang Xia, a former professor at Peking University and a political dissident from China.
Mr. Xia has been sued for his inquiries and criticism through TV and twitter on Guo’s so-called exposure of top confidential information in China by Wengui Guo (aka Miles Kwok, a notorious Chinese billionaire and fugitive escaped from China in 2015 and Guo got RED NOTICE twice from INTERPOL) at Eastern District Court of Virginia.
Guo hired a gang of cyber accessories and made up tons of rumors to smear Mr. Xia and Xia’s family members while filing a complaint against Xia with an accusation of defamation and a claim of five million US $ for compensation.
Guo has been abusing legal resources in US with more than 41 lawsuits for defamation undergoing and he claimed that he planned to sue more than 91 persons for the accusation of defamation.
Mr. Xia and many other defendants can’t afford to hire a qualified and experienced attorney to defend themselves. Thus, with suggestions by many web bystanders, Xia started a campaign to collect donation for legal fees against Guo.
Xia will use those donations only for the purpose of the lawsuit and he has been supported by several volunteers to work on collection, bookkeeping and supervision of donations. The goal has been set to 100,000 US$, and an individual account of GoFundMe was set up as a major channel for donation.
Please contact Julia Lee and other volunteers through [email redacted] for the details.
We’re most grateful to your attention, encouragement, support and great help!
原北大教授、政治异议人士，现时政/财经新闻评论人夏业良先生（美国之音/自由亚洲电台/博讯/新唐人等媒体）因网络质疑和评论，而被中国逃亡商人郭文贵花钱组织围攻/抹黑，并在美国弗吉尼亚东区联邦法院提交所谓诽谤指控和滥诉。
夏先生通过电视节目和推特对郭的所谓爆料（包括最高机密信息）进行了质疑和批评，郭雇佣组织了对夏及其家人的网络围攻，同时指控夏对他进行诽谤并索赔五百万美元。
郭滥用美国司法资源， 目前正在进行中的诉讼超过41起，郭宣称他计划起诉至少91位对他进行诽谤的个人。
夏先生和其他被告均无力承担雇佣合格并有经验的律师之花费。因此在众多网络旁观者的建议下开始了募捐应对郭之诉讼的律师费用。
夏先生将把募捐得款只用于本案诉讼之中，并且得到若干志愿者的支持和帮助，他们协助收集募捐款项/记账与募捐监督等工作。本次募捐活动的目标已设定为十万美元，并且已经开设了一个名为“GoFundMe”之软件的募捐账户平台以作为主要募捐渠道。
请各位捐助者通过电子邮箱：[email redacted] 与Julia Lee等志愿者联系，以获得相关细节。

content:
Fundraiser by Heather Liu : Help A #MeToo Survivor and Daughter Win Their Case
Heather Liu is organizing this fundraiser.
What I’ve experienced isn’t what any woman should ever go through. First there was the violence of non-consensual sex forced on me, followed by lies and denial. Then, rare moments of hope, followed by setbacks tinged with revenge from a father whose fear of revealing truth drives him to deny his child’s existence. This child is my daughter. For 20 years I’ve hidden the nightmare involving her origin by my silence, partly due to the sense of shame and partly because the father of my child is a influential public figure. Till the rapist has pushed us to a corner by threatening our existence with vicious conspiracy theories.
（我經歷了任何一位女性都不該經歷的事情。先是遭遇性侵，接著還要面對謊言、抵賴和詆毀。過去20年來，間或閃現的希望，卻因我女兒的生父拒絕承認這孩子的存在，而淹沒在長久的幻滅中。過去20年來，我一直對女兒的身世三緘其口，讓一段揮之不去的夢魘深藏內心，一方面出於羞辱感，另一方面無法面對孩子的生父作為一個公眾人物給我心靈帶來的扭曲。）
With your help, the truth of our experience will be told. When it is, I hope justice will prevail. This is why I’m emerging from the shadows.
（因您伸出援手，我將得以說出這段真實的經歷。當真相大白的那一天到來，我希望正義能夠隨之彰顯。）
In 2000, I was a journalist working for a local Chinese newspaper in Los Angeles. I was assigned to interview a famous Chinese dissident, a political refugee in America, who people called the “Godfather of the Democratic Movement in China.” I wrote the story, but in doing so, my life was changed forever by his sexual assault of me.
（2000年，身為洛杉磯當地一家中文媒體記者的我，被派去採訪一位著名的中國異議人士，也是我本人非常敬仰的政治流亡者、一位被視為「中國民主運動之父」的風雲人物。我完成了採訪任務，然而我的個人生活卻因今生與他這唯一的遭逢而徹底脫軌。）
Let’s just say, nine months after I did that story, I gave birth to my daughter, who bore no resemblance to my then-husband. My husband knew why since I’d told him about the sexual assault after it happened. My marriage ended, and my life as a single mom began. To protect my daughter and me from possible backlash about how she was conceived and her father’s identity, I kept my ordeal quiet. The two of us moved to Hong Kong.
（在我做了那次採訪的9個月之後，我的女兒降生了。她跟我當時的丈夫長得一點也不像，而我丈夫也並不感到驚訝，因為我早跟他坦白了我遭遇性侵的事。我的婚姻其實從那時起已名存實亡，我作為一個單親母親的生涯也即將開始。為了遠離各種因孩子身世而產生的猜忌，讓我和孩子可以過安靜而屬於自己的生活，同時也為了可以就近得到父母家人的幫忙照顧，我帶著孩子離開了美國，赴香港尋找發展機會。）
Through the years I never thought about contacting my daughter's biological father, whom I met only once. I didn’t consider doing this even after I lost my job as an editor in 2012. But then a former colleague, Beifeng, left Hong Kong for the United States. He’d criticized me for "depriving the child the right to be recognized by her father," and later persuaded me to let him bring a lock of my daughter’s hair, wrapped it in tissue paper, that he took with him to the United States.
（多年來，我從未想過要聯絡孩子的生父，那個我只見過一面的人，哪怕是2012年我失業的時候也沒萌生這個打算。我根本已經忘記了這個人，要不是當時正要動身赴美的前同事北風（我告訴了他我的孩子生父是誰，但沒有讓他知道詳情，他也沒有探問）批評我「剝奪孩子認父的權利」。他太太當即揪了孩子幾根頭髮，用手紙包了起來。）
Months later, my heart sank when Beifeng reported back to me that this man had denied everything, even the possibility of knowing me, let alone the possibility of having fathered a child. He’d committed this horrible crime against me, but he refused to acknowledge this truth. For to accept that he’d fathered a daughter, he’d have to admit how she came to existence. It appeared that he was refusing to allow his carefully crafted story about his “heroic” life to be marred by acknowledging his daughter’s existence.
（幾個月之後，北風帶來消息並深表意外地說，孩子的生父得知自己可能有個孩子時的反應，竟是敷衍和閃躲，好像根本不可能有這回事一樣。他當然寧肯忘記自己做過的事，但真相怎麼能因你不想面對就可以不承認、孩子怎麼可以就這樣當她不存在呢？就像他後來在郵件裡提到的，他所關切的，是這事將來在他的回憶錄裡該怎麼寫，而不是他身為人父應該盡什麼責。他在意的只是他自己英雄般的人生，無論如何不能留下任何污點。）
After this news reached me, I was diagnosed with clinical depression and started to see a doctor regularly. Professionally, however, I had to appear calm and collected so I could earn a living that would support the two of us. I worked as a freelance writer and translator, while also raising my daughter on my own.
（我聞訊心裡沉了一下，不久開始意識恍惚，甚至試過下班下車記不起回家的方向。我遠在北京的母親聽說之後，在電話的另一頭啜泣得聲音哽咽。2013年2月，我被確診患上抑鬱症。失業更兼病倒，令我們母女的生計雪上加霜，這期間我成為自由撰稿人，還要硬撐著努力譯書維持生計。好在偶爾有父母幫手、妹妹接濟一下，才度過了一段危機。）
Five years later, in 2018, in the midst of #MeToo movement, when sexual abuse and harassment were receiving public attention globally, rumors spread online about this famous Chinese man having fathered an illegitimate child. At that point, I contacted him by phone from Hong Kong and boldly asked for child support.
（一晃又過了5年，時間到了2018年，在#MeToo（「我也是受害者」）運動的聲浪中，性侵和性騷擾現象的普遍存在引起了全球性輿論關注。在此期間，網上首次出現了對我女兒的生父「不認親」的議論。已變得反應遲緩的我這才開始應對，邁出了主動聯繫孩子生父這一步。）
He agreed to a DNA test that was performed privately in Washington D.C.., The DNA results proved that he was Charlotte's father. The person who shared the results with him said that he had responded positively to having a daughter. Accordingly, when I contacted him again, he promised to assist us by at least paying for her education. But later on, since I would not change my tone on the unhappy encounter with him in the past, he decided to deny being Charlotte’s father and began to challenge the DNA results, shirked his responsibility as her biological father, and ignored that I was a victim of his violent sexual assault.
（他於是主動提出做個DNA鑑定，並指定了一位背景相當可靠的前白宮幕僚做中間人，在華盛頓特區進行了DNA樣本的收集與鑑定。結果出來後，中間人率先通知我，說結果證明魏先生是孩子的生父無疑，並告訴我，魏先生對鑑定結果表示認可並顯得「很開心」。據此，在我與孩子的生父再次聯繫時，他表示自己起碼會負擔孩子的大學學費。但真到了時候他又變卦了，甚至仗著沒有把DNA鑑定結果如約給我們，便想將已經做過DNA鑑定這事也想賴掉。）
The rest of the story is detailed in Huaizhao Liu v. Jingsheng Wei, case #1:19-cv-03344, which was heard in the Washington, D.C. federal court. Charlotte’s father managed to find the funds necessary to hire a high-powered defense attorney to help him to deny both our dignity and his basic obligations of paternity.
（後來的事情見華盛頓特區聯邦法院卷宗（Case Number 1:19-cv-03344）。我女兒的生父大手筆聘請了專攻白領犯罪辯護的名牌大狀為自己的辯護律師，竭力搬弄法律條文進行技術性規避，想就此永遠掩蓋真相，踐踏我們母女的權益與尊嚴。）
We believe that Charlotte’s biological father should be forced to keep his promise of supporting her education, and we are asking that he release the DNA test results to us. His 19-year old daughter deserves to know the truth.
（我們堅信，法庭應該為這位竭力否認已經做過親子鑑定的生父驗明正身，然後強制他履行他的諾言，承擔他女兒的學費。我們堅信，他19歲的女兒有權利知曉真相。）
The weight of evidence is on our side, but we risk losing the lawsuit that we are filing against him if we cannot raise the money we need to hire an attorney who is as capable as his lawyer. What is at risk is Charlotte's right to a quality education, along with the legally binding acknowledgement of his paternity.
（儘管我們掌握活生生的證據，但如果籌不到聘請律師的費用，單憑我們自訴，將無法應對複雜的陪審團庭審程序。立案至今一年多來，被告採取躲和拖的戰術，先是躲傳票，然後提出「司法管轄權」爭議逼我們撤案，一計不成又援引「多國籍」條款，將案子從特區高等法院轉移到聯邦法院。）
With your assistance – with your contributions – we intend to hire an attorney who is experienced in sexual assault and paternity cases. We hope to win this #MeToo case and pursue respectful, equal and democratic human relationship in Chinese community.
（您的捐助將幫助我們聘請到專攻性侵案和親子案官司的律師，幫我們贏得這場事關尊嚴、平等、人權以及人性的人身傷害官司，並藉此推動美國的華人社區乃至全球華人的觀念進步與行為的現代化。）
Here are some online stories and commentary about this, in Chinese:
https://www.storm.mg/article/2891777?mode=whole
(by Liao Yiwu, award winner of Human Rights Watch Hellman-Hammett Grant 2003, the German Geschwister-Scholl-Preis 2011 and the Peace Prize of the German Book Trade 2012.)
（作者/廖亦武，詩人、流亡作家與底層歷史記錄者。2012年德國書業和平獎得主，並曾獲美國《當代基督教》雜誌頒發的「最佳圖書奬」、德國書業協會頒發的「紹爾兄妹獎」、德國廣播協會頒發的「最佳廣播劇奬」及德國阿夏芬堡頒發的「公民勇氣奬」。2013年，法國政府頒發給廖亦武「法蘭西文學藝術軍官獎章」。2018年，廖亦武獲美國紐約瓦茨拉夫 哈維爾圖書基金會頒發「無懼危難作家獎」。）
http://minzhuzhongguo.org/MainArtShow.aspx?AID=105641
(by Qi JIazhen, writer in exile, author of autobiographical series: Tears of the Goddess of Liberty and Red Dog. Qi is the Chairwoman of the Women Writers committee, Independent Chinese PEN Center.)
（作者/齊家貞，流亡作家，著有系列傳記《自由神的眼泪──父女两代囚徒的真實故事》（後改名《黑牆裡的倖存者》和《紅狗：—個被釋女囚的真實故事》在香港和台灣出版。齊家貞曾先後擔任國際筆會獨立中文筆會理事會理事、副會長、秘書長等職務，並在澳洲建立了“齊氏文化基金會”，每年頒發“推動中國進步獎”截至2019年已連續頒獎12屆。）
https://liuvswei.blogspot.com/2020/08/metoo.html
(by Lau Kayee, Chairwoman of Network for Women In Politics, Hong Kong; Spokeswoman of Hong Kong Civil Human Rights Front.)
（作者/劉家儀，香港婦女參政網絡主席，六四新生代秘書長，支聯會常委，香港市民捍衛人權陣線發言人。）
With your contributions, we will be able to set a positive example for #MeToo victims by raising awareness about women’s and children's rights, globally.
因您的資助，我們將能夠為#MeToo運動傷害者們建立一個積極的個案，為提高女性及孩童的權利意識而有所貢獻。

content:
Fundraiser by Boston Standswithhk : US Hong Kong Safe Harbor Postcard Campaign
Boston Standswithhk is organizing this fundraiser.
***When donation, make as anonymous if you wish to hide the donator's name and make the TIPS to 0.00***
While US-China tensions continue to escalate and the November presidential elections loom near, as Hongkongers living in the United States (or any informed person in the world), we must not forget or turn a blind eye to the CCP’s continuous oppression on Hongkongers and other minority groups in China, such as Uyghurs, Tibetans, and Mongolians. With the promulgation of the new National Security Law on June 30, 2020, the government has since been arresting and charging dissidents with these vaguely-worded laws that may entail life imprisonment. In the past month alone, 12 Hong Kongers fleeing protest-related charges have been detained in China and denied meetings with lawyers since August 23, 2020; Legislative Council elections had been postponed a year in the name of “public health concerns” amidst a mass arrest of candidates; media mogul Jimmy Lai, who runs the only pro-democratic print newspaper in Hong Kong, has been arrested with the National Security Law; and the Education Bureau has begun actively censoring content they deemed politically incorrect in Liberal Studies textbooks, including concepts like “civil disobedience” and “separation of powers”, and images of Lennon Walls. Up until today, the administration has arrested more than 10,000 Hong Kongers, charged over 2,200, deployed water cannons, fired more than 16,000 tear gas canisters and over 10,000 rubber bullets against its own people. Freedom of speech, freedom of assembly and political rights as we knew it have been thoroughly eroded.
11月的美國總統大選逐漸逼近，中美關係日漸緊張，作為居住在美國的香港人或是在這個世界上任何有良知的人，面對中共對香港、維吾爾族、藏族和蒙古族的持續壓逼，我們不能容忍，更不能視而不見。自2020年6月30日頒布《國家安全法》以來，政府持續逮捕異見人​​士，並以措辭含糊的法律起訴抗爭者，香港的司法制度已經徹底淪為政府的打壓工具。及後更有12名香港抗爭者為了逃離這種不公義的審判欲流亡台灣，卻被中共非法拘捕。他們無法與律師會面，音訊全無。而香港人僅有的發聲方法——立法會選舉，卻因為「公共衛生風險」而被推遲一年；同時間，大批候選人被逮捕或是被拒絕參選。作為香港唯一異見紙媒《蘋果日報》的老闆黎智英被警方高調逮捕，《蘋果日報》總部更被大肆搜查。教育局亦積極審查通識科教科書中所謂的「政治不正確」內容，例如「公民抗命」和「三權分立」的概念，以及連儂牆相片。到今天為止，已經有超過10,000多名香港人被捕、2,200多人被起訴，警方向市民發射了超過16,000枚催淚彈和10,000多發橡皮子彈，令香港人長期生活在恐懼中。香港人的言論自由、集會自由和政治權利已被徹底侵蝕。
In light of the deteriorating situation, we plan to kickstart a new round of postcard campaign urging Congress to pass two bills related to Hong Kong as soon as possible - Hong Kong Safe Harbor Act (H.R.7415/S.4110), and Hong Kong People’s Freedom and Choice Act (H.R.7428/S.4229):
鑑於情況日益惡化，我們希望透過郵寄明信片給國會議員的方式，呼籲他們盡快通過兩項與香港有關的法案 —— 香港安全港法案 (H.R.7415 / S.4110) 和香港人民自由與選擇法(H.R.7428 / S.4229):
The Hong Kong Safe Harbor Act will designate certain Hong Kong residents who are victims of persecution or who have a well-founded fear of future persecution because of their peaceful political activities as Priority 2 refugees (excluded from refugee cap), allowing them and their spouses, children, parents to apply to the U.S. Refugee Admissions Program for protection. (Click here for more details)
《香港安全港法案》將指定某些遭受迫害，或因其參與和平的政治活動而感到恐懼的香港居民列為「優先級別2」的難民，且不受每年限額限制，亦允許他們及其配偶、子女、父母向「美國難民接納計劃」申請庇護。(詳情請瀏覽)
The Hong Kong People's Freedom and Choice Act will provide Temporary Protected Status (TPS) for Hong Kongers, maintain Hong Kong’s status as autonomous for the purposes of immigration, provide special and expedited status for certain high-skilled Hong Kongers as well as expedite Permanent Resident status for Hong Kongers residing in the US. (Click here for more details)
《香港人民自由與選擇法》會為香港人提供臨時保護身份（TPS），維持香港在移民方面的自治地位，亦為部分香港專業人仕提供特殊和快速的身份，並加快辦理香港人的美國永久居民(綠卡)身份的程序。(詳情請瀏覽)
In our last postcard campaign pushing for the Hong Kong Human Rights and Democracy Act, we delivered over 3000 postcards to Congress. We aren’t part of any formal organization and do not have operation funds. We desperately call for your contribution again to help us deliver these postcards to Congress, to remind them of Hong Kong’s urgent situation and urge them to take immediate action. Your contribution would support our printing and delivery costs. Thank you so much!
在上一次推動《香港人權與民主法》的明信片運動中，我們向國會送出了超過3000張的明信片。我們不是任何正式組織的成員，也沒有運營資金，所以我們竭誠呼籲您為我們提供資金，並幫助我們將這些明信片送交您們所屬的國會議員，提醒他們香港的緊急狀況，並呼籲他們立即採取行動。所有受到的捐款將支持我們的打印和交付成本。萬分感謝！

Fundraiser by Alan Wan : Help Alan Navigate Life in Political Exile
Alan’s fund provides groceries and rent for a political dissident facing exile abroad
Inspire others and help Alan build momentum.
Inspire others and help Alan build momentum.
Alan Wan is organizing this fundraiser.
My name is Alan, and I am writing this with a sincere and humble heart.
I am a Chinese political dissident living in Houston, Texas. Because of my beliefs and my willingness to speak openly about freedom, human rights, and justice, I have faced serious threats and intimidation from the Chinese government. These pressures have made it impossible for me to safely return to China, where my family still lives. Every day, I carry the pain of being separated from my loved ones, uncertain when—or if—I will ever be able to reunite with them again.
Beyond the emotional suffering, I am now facing severe financial hardship. Due to restrictions and complications surrounding the transfer of my personal funds from abroad, I have been unable to access resources that I once depended on for survival. My savings are rapidly disappearing, and I am now struggling simply to cover basic daily necessities such as food, housing, transportation, and medical care.
This situation has left me feeling isolated and vulnerable. I never imagined that standing by my principles would lead to such profound personal sacrifice, but I continue to hold onto hope.
Today, I am reaching out with deep humility to ask for your support. Any assistance—whether financial help, practical resources, or connections to organizations that aid individuals in political exile—would mean more than words can express. Your kindness could help me maintain stability during this incredibly difficult chapter of my life and allow me to continue moving forward with dignity.
I am not asking for luxury, only for the chance to live safely and meet my most basic needs while I navigate these extraordinary challenges.
Thank you for taking the time to read my story. Your compassion, understanding, and support would be a lifeline during one of the hardest periods of my life.
Grocery and part of my rent.

Fundraiser by Pie Formosa : Support Pie Formosa’s Independent Work
Inspire others and help Pie build momentum.
Inspire others and help Pie build momentum.
Pie Formosa is organizing this fundraiser.
I sometimes describe myself as a refugee from WeChat to Instagram — but I am also, quite literally, a refugee from China.
I am a political dissident, human rights activist, non-binary person and independent writer living with invisible disabilities, now continuing my work in Europe.
I write and create public work about censorship, authoritarianism, political memory, democracy, queer and trans freedom, refugee experiences, neurodiversity, and the cultural spaces where resistance survives.
For years, WeChat was one of the places where I published my work. Readers could easily support independent creators with small tips. Then the Chinese Communist Party shut down my account. I lost not only a platform, but also an audience, an archive, and a simple way for people to support my work.
This fundraiser is part of rebuilding that independence.
Living with invisible disabilities also means that conventional employment structures and constant high-intensity workloads are not always accessible or sustainable for me. I need a modest and stable income to make independent research, writing and human-rights work sustainable.
* research, writing and documentation
* travel to human-rights, democracy and civil-society events
* basic living costs that allow me to continue this work independently
If something I have written, documented or created has informed, helped or inspired you, even €1, €5 or €10 helps me keep this work alive. If donating is not possible, sharing this fundraiser also makes a real difference.
Authoritarianism depends on silence and forgetting. Independent voices survive because people choose to keep them alive.
Thank you for supporting my work.

summary: Fundraiser by Mark Nygate : SAVE US FROM THE MEGA EMBASSY! SUPPORT OUR LEGAL CHALLENGE Mark Nygate is organizing this fundraiser. We are 100 families taking on the CCP - and we need your help. 我們是「皇家鑄幣廠居民協會」，由約一百戶職工家庭組成。我們懇請你伸出援手。 In 2018,
content:
Fundraiser by Mark Nygate : SAVE US FROM THE MEGA EMBASSY! SUPPORT OUR LEGAL CHALLENGE
Mark Nygate is organizing this fundraiser.
We are 100 families taking on the CCP - and we need your help.
我們是「皇家鑄幣廠居民協會」，由約一百戶職工家庭組成。我們懇請你伸出援手。
In 2018, our homes-key-worker flats in Tower Hamlets were sold in a secretive deal to the People's Republic of China. We had no say. No warning. And now, we face living under the shadow of a hostile superpower.
2018年，我們居住的Tower Hamlets地段，在未經通知、無任何諮詢下，被秘密售予中國政府。我們無從置喙，如今更面對一個敵對政權的威脅。
The UK Government is expected to approve plans to build the largest embassy in Europe - right here, at Royal Mint Court, next to the Tower of London… and directly on top of our homes.
英國政府即將批准於倫敦塔旁的皇家鑄幣廠（Royal Mint Court）興建歐洲最大規模的中國大使館，預定地點正正位於我們所居之上。
This is not just a planning dispute.
我們擔憂的不僅是一項城市規劃決策，而是一場關乎國家安全、人身安全與基本權利的危機。
China has never shown any regard for our safety - and now the Government and the Metropolitan Police have abandoned us too.
自2018年起，中國政府從未就此提供明確回應，我們甚至不知道會否被驅逐、是否仍能繼續安居於此。而如今，政府與執法機關也對我們置之不理。
We are the Royal Mint Court Residents Association. People backed our previous Crowdfunder campaign that helped pay for a barrister to present our evidence including an independent security assessment showing the serious risks to us from a terror attack on the mega-embassy.
我們是「皇家鑄幣廠居民協會」。我們之前的眾籌活動獲得許多人的支持，資助我們聘請資深大律師提交證據，包括一份獨立的安全評估報告，指出超級大使館可能帶來的恐襲風險。
We are now launching an urgent legal challenge - a Judicial Review - to change the law and stop this injustice.
我們現在正展開一項緊急法律挑戰 — 即司法覆核 — 希望改變現行法律，阻止這場不公。
We need your help to protect our community from the mighty Chinese Communist Party.
我們需要你的幫助，去保護我們的社區，免受強大的中國共產黨威脅。
Whatever you can spare us, will help David stand-up to Goliath.
We are seeking to pursue a Judicial Review because we have believed all along that the planning process has been flawed. Here are some of the reasons we think are likely to be relevant:
我們決定提起司法覆核，是因為我們始終認為整個規劃程序存在問題。以下是我們認為可能相關的一些原因：
“Closed mind”: Ministers may have signalled early approval to China, before formal procedures were followed, breaking the law and abusing planning powers. In a similar vein, objections disappeared after UK ministers returned from Beijing. Residents have felt like pawns in a geopolitical game since the start.
預設立場：部長們可能在正式程序開始前就向中方表示支持，違反法律並濫用規劃權力。在部長們從北京回來之後，原有的反對聲音突然消失。居民們從一開始就覺得自己成了地緣政治博弈中的棋子。
Security concerns: Building a fortified embassy with homes on site and critical infrastructure nearby, ignoring espionage concerns and the real human risk to dissidents, is indefensible.
安全隱患：在住宅區內及重要基礎設施附近建設高度防禦的大使館，無視間諜活動與對異見人士的人身威脅，完全不能接受。
Procedural unfairness: We were shut out of the process. No consultation. No transparency. No respect for the people who live here.
程序不公：我們被完全排除在決策過程之外。無諮詢、無透明、無對居民的尊重。
Legitimate expectation: We were promised due process and protection. We got silence.
合理期望落空：我們被承諾將獲程序保障與保護，實際卻是得不到任何保障。
We still live here. 100 families. Nurses, teachers, pensioners. Our 100 homes are on land now owned by the Chinese government. That means the Chinese ambassador is our landlord - with rights to enter our homes.
我們仍然住在這裡 ，足足一百戶家庭，包括護士、教師、退休人士。我們的一百個住所現已位於中國政府擁有的土地上。這代表中國大使成為我們的業主，有權進入我們的住所。
China refuses to answer us. Since 2018, we’ve begged for assurances: will we be evicted? Will we be safe? Can we stay? Beijing’s answer: not until we get planning permission. This refusal, and the proposal to install a temporary style wooden boundary fence as a dividing line, raises fears that the Chinese Government intends to take back the entire 100 apartments at St Mary Graces Court once they secure diplomatic status for the site, leaving us homeless.
中國拒絕回應我們的訴求。自2018年起，我們不斷尋求保證：我們會被驅逐嗎？我們是否安全？我們能否繼續居住？北京的答覆是：等規劃許可下來再說。這種拒絕，以及擬議中以臨時木欄分隔的做法，讓我們擔心中國政府一旦取得外交地位，將會收回整個St Mary Graces Court的100個單位，使我們流離失所。
This embassy is a fortress. It’s not a normal diplomatic building. It will have secret communications centres, fortified walls, and surveillance technology that can monitor our entire estate, even our bedrooms. It will also stand on top of critical UK cables that MI5 warn are a security risk to the UK.
這座大使館是一個堡壘，並非普通的外交建築。它將設有秘密通訊設施、加固圍牆、監控技術，可監視整個屋苑，甚至包括我們的睡房。而它的地基下方，更有英國重要電纜 ，MI5曾警告這是對國家安全的威脅。
The UK Government knows the risk - and ignored it. Our independent security report warns that this site puts families and national security at risk. Even the UK’s Head of Counter-Terrorism originally objected - citing threats to residents and dissidents. But since ministers returned from Beijing, objections have mysteriously vanished.
英國政府明知有風險，卻選擇無視。我們的獨立安全報告指出，該地點將危害居民與國家安全。甚至連英國反恐部門首長最初也曾反對 ， 指出對居民與異見人士的威脅。但自從部長從北京回來後，這些反對聲音神秘地消失。
Ministers made no mention of the 100 families living here. We are alarmed that the letters from Home Secretary Yvette Cooper and Foreign Secretary David Lammy have ignored the fact that UK families live in 100 apartments on the land that is actually part of Royal Mint court - and is owned by the Chinese government. Our Resident’s Chairman has personally appealed to ministers, submitted the full Crilly Consultants security report, and our plight has appeared in The Times, FT, BBC, CNN, and more. What is happening to democratic accountability in this country?
部長們從未提及這裡有一百戶居民。我們對內政大臣Yvette Cooper及外交大臣David Lammy的信件感到震驚，因為他們完全忽略了皇家鑄幣廠的土地上住有英國公民、100個家庭。我們的居民協會主席曾親自致函部長、提交完整的Crilly安全報告，而我們的處境亦已被《泰晤士報》、《金融時報》、BBC、CNN等多間媒體報導。英國民主問責制度何在？
The first duty of the UK government is to protect its citizens. We understand the UK’s diplomatic obligations - but not at the expense of its own people. The refusal to acknowledge the basic risks of housing a high-security foreign embassy on top of a residential block is deeply troubling. It appears the government is prioritising relations with Beijing over the safety of its own citizens.
英國政府的首要職責是保護其國民。我們明白外交義務，但不能以犧牲本國人民為代價。將一個高安全級別的外國大使館設於住宅區上方，而拒絕承認基本風險，是極度令人不安的。
It’s not just about us. Dissidents, including Hong Kongers, Uyghurs, Tibetans, Taiwanese and Chinese exile communities are terrified. They’ve told us they no longer feel safe protesting outside the site, and on British soil. Their presence, and ours, will be met with constant surveillance and intimidation by a regime known to harass and threaten activists - even abroad.
這件事不僅關係到我們。流亡港人、維吾爾人、西藏人、台灣人及中國異見社群皆感到恐懼。他們表示不再敢在該地點或英國土地上公開抗議。他們與我們一樣，將面對來自這個以恐嚇異見者聞名的政權的持續監控與威嚇。
The people have spoken, and they support us.
On 8 February 2025, thousands of British citizens - including Hong Kongers, Uyghurs, Tibetans, Taiwanese and Chinese pro-democracy activists, and human rights campaigners - gathered outside Royal Mint Court in protest against this embassy.
2025年2月8日，數以千計的英國公民 ，包括港人、維吾爾人、西藏人、台灣人、中國民主人士與人權倡議者， 齊集皇家鑄幣廠，抗議中國大使館計劃。
They were joined by cross-party MPs, journalists, and allies. Together, they said NO to the Chinese embassy, and YES to democratic values, safety, and justice.
他們與跨黨派議員、記者及盟友並肩站立，一同說出明確立場：反對中國大使館，支持民主、安全與公義。
Further mass protests followed on 15 March, 3 May, and 14 June - showing growing national resistance to the plan.
3月15日、5月3日及6月14日亦舉行後續大型集會，反對聲浪日益壯大。
They continue to protest, and have made it clear: they won’t stop until this mega-embassy deal is over.
抗議仍在持續，並清楚表示：他們不會停止，直至該項目取消為止。
But the Government is not listening.
But we need your help - fast.
The legal fees for a Judicial Review are beyond the reach of ordinary families. But with your help, we can stand up to both Beijing and Whitehall.
司法覆核的法律費用遠超普通家庭的負擔。但在您的幫助下，我們能夠與北京和英國政府對抗。
This case is about more than one building. It’s about:
Protecting British citizens from state overreach
Defending UK democracy from foreign influence
Challenging backroom deals that put power over people
If we succeed, we won’t just protect our homes. We’ll set a precedent that no foreign government can build on British soil without respecting British citizens and British values.
如若成功，我們不僅能保護我們的家園，我們更是創下先例：任何外國政府不得在罔顧英國公民和英國價值的前提下在英國土地上建造任何建築。
Please chip in whatever you can. £10. £100. £1,000. Every penny goes to legal costs to take this to court. We are a group of teachers, nurses, shop workers and pensioners. We don’t have the Chinese Communist Party’s millions - but with your help, we do have people power.
請您捐出任何您能負擔的金額 — 不論是 £10，£100 還是 £1,000。每一分錢都將用於支付法律費用，讓我們將此案帶上法庭。我們只是一群教師、護士、店員和退休人士。雖然我們沒有中國共產黨的龐大資金 — 但在您的幫助下，我們擁有的是人民的力量。
Because if they can do this to us, they can do it to anyone.
This is a secure UK-based platform, fully registered and subject to UK law.
It is widely used to support political and legal campaigns, including by MPs, NGOs, and grassroots movements - some of which are openly critical of the Chinese government.
該平台廣泛用於支持政治和法律活動，包括國會議員、非政府組織和基層運動 — 包括曾公開批評中國政府的政治活動。
The platform offers full transparency, with public donation records and payment processing via Stripe or PayPal.
該平台提供完全透明的捐款記錄，並通過 Stripe 或 PayPal 處理支付。
There is no history of censorship or compliance with pressure from the Chinese state.
It adheres strictly to GDPR regulations, ensuring donor and campaigner data is protected.
平台嚴格遵守 GDPR 規範，確保捐款者和活動者的數據安全。
2.95% + 0.25 of each donation goes to the platform; 100% of the remaining funds will be used to cover legal costs.
每筆捐款將扣除 2.95% 加 £0.25 之平台手續費，其餘款項將全數用以支付法律相關費用。
If the legal case is dismissed, your donation will be directed to charity unless you request a refund. If you would like your donation returned, please email us. We will calculate and refund your contribution (with platform fee deducted).
如法律訴訟最終被駁回，捐款將撥捐予慈善機構，除非閣下主動申請退款。如欲索回捐款，請電郵至，我們將在扣除平台手續費後，計算並退還閣下之捐款。
We will post updates every two weeks, which you can follow directly on this page.

content:
Fundraiser by Luke Rudkowski : Fund Independent Reporting In HONG KONG
Luke Rudkowski is organizing this fundraiser.
You know something big is happening in Hong Kong!! The protests have been massive, and they may be the biggest geopolitical event of the year. Will China get its way and stomp out dissent? Might covert U.S. aid allow the protesters to sustain their momentum? Needless to say, there is a lot at stake and lots of speculation!!
And because of that it’s important for there to be independent, on-the-ground reporting about the events in Hong Kong.
When massive Yellow Vests protests were taking place in Paris, We Are Change was there reporting on the ground and risking safety as protesters were losing eyes due to police brutality. In the past we have also been to places likeSomalia, Venezuela and Cheran , once the most violent, dangerous area in Mexico.
As for Hong Kong, it’s very expensive to fly and stay there. This mission will involve spending a week or more investigating, reporting and live-streaming.
So if you value reporting on the events in Hong Kong that is independent and free of spin and manipulation, then your support is crucial! By contributing to this campaign, you will help fund the cost of the flight, safety precautions and live reporting at events like the upcoming Civil Human Rights Front March on August 31 and the student strike that is set to take place on September 2, the first day of secondary school.
Our $2,700 goal is the bare minimum it will take to fund this trip. If we surpass the goal due to your support, which is so greatly appreciated, the funds will go toward other journalistic endeavors. Thank you so much! Your support means the world to us!

content:
Belize Jungle & Island Glamping Adventure Tour, Sun, Nov 29, 2026, 7:00 AM | Meetup
Belize Jungle & Island Glamping Adventure Tour
Join our Belize Jungle Adventure Tour & Glamping adventure trip for women only! Spend 8 glorious days staying active in a tropical paradise! Explore the rainforest jungle, try waterfall rappelling, discover ancient Mayan ruins, snorkel, zip-line, and more! Enjoy all of this, plus luxurious glamping on a remote Caribbean island.
Trade endless staff meetings for a heart-thumping collision of mainland jungle exploration and tropical island glamping on a UNESCO-designated Marine Preserve?! Forgive us, but you aren’t going to BELIZE this trip.
Your adventure in Belize will encompass the best adrenaline-pumping jungle activities on the mainland and the serene, remote island experience in the middle of the Caribbean Sea on a UNESCO-designated Marine Preserve.
During the first half of your jungle adventure, you’ll explore Mayan ruins, navigate caves featuring 3,000-year-old artifacts, and immerse yourself in the Belizean Jungle embarking on new adventures each day.
WATERFALL RAPPELLING, ZIP-LINING, AND CAVING
Learn to rappel and descend 250 feet from the top of a waterfall with views as far as the turquoise Caribbean Sea. Zip-line 2.5 miles through Bocawina National Park over the jungle canopy enjoying Belize from a bird’s eye view. Then, channel your inner Indiana Jones as you strap on your headlamp and step back in time 3,000 years into the depths of a cave with Mayan artifacts and ceremonial alters.
To top it off, wander the archaeological grounds of Xunantunich. An ancient civilization of over 200,000 people thrived here until 1,000 years ago, when it was mysteriously abandoned. During your adventures on the mainland, stay in a Rainforest Eco-Lodge powered completely by hydroelectricity and solar with your gang of Explorer Chick gal pals.
SNORKELING, KAYAKING, AND SUP
On the second half of your Belize Jungle Tour Adventure, we’ll whisk you away from the mainland! Travel by boat 36 miles to a remote island Glamping base camp for the next 5 days and 4 nights.
Glover’s Reef Marine Preserve is designated as a UNESCO World Heritage Site and is one of only four atolls in the western hemisphere. The turquoise waters are host to over 700 patch reefs. It is one of the richest tropical marine environments in the Caribbean. The waters here are exceptionally clear because of its isolation from the mainland making it a utopia for spotting marine life and water activities. Hello, coral reefs and all the fishies! 🐠
Fill your days with water activities exploring your remote island paradise. Grab snorkel gear and head out on a SUP to swim with sea turtles and colorful fish. Learn to use the wind to your advantage and kayak sail to coral destinations. Master the technique of line fishing from local Belizean guides and cook up your catch for dinner. Or, just kick it in a hammock with a good book as the wind rocks you gently. Oh, and you bet there will be dance parties as you learn Garifuna moves.💃
PRIVATE, REMOTE ISLAND GLAMPING
So, what really makes these last five days special? Your home away from home on a remote, 13-acre island! These digs are Pinterest-worthy tent-walled cabanas with real beds, wooden floors, a porch, and that essential ocean view right outside your screened door. 👌 Go to sleep each night to the sound of the sea lapping the shore from your Cabana.
Wake up each day to views of the Caribbean and learn a new definition of paradise. Embrace the Belizean way of life devoid of chaos and spend your days on Ocean Time. This is not to say our days will be spent like a fly and flop vacation, tanning on the beach. Heck no! Your days will be filled with the perfect amount of activity and relaxation to give you the ultimate and authentic Caribbean Island experience off the coast of Belize.

summary: Fundraiser by Hillary Johnson : Hong Kong Photojournalism Trip Hillary Johnson is organizing this fundraiser. Hi everyone, my name is Hillary Johnson, and I’m a photographer living in Chicago, working all over the Midwest and in Hong Kong.
content:
Fundraiser by Hillary Johnson : Hong Kong Photojournalism Trip
Hillary Johnson is organizing this fundraiser.
Hi everyone, my name is Hillary Johnson, and I’m a photographer living in Chicago, working all over the Midwest and in Hong Kong. I have two main threads to my photography practice, photojournalism and fine art.
Though it feels awkward, I confess, I’m pushing ahead because I need your help.
I’m going to Hong Kong on November 12 to cover the protest and the election of a new cabinet in Hong Kong.
You might wonder why bother giving money to me or why my voice particular needs to be added to this news event, or even why this matters to you at all. I hear that and I’ll do my best to answer your questions. I’ll also explain what you can do if you’re interested in helping out.
A little bit about me: in addition to being a photographer I’m also someone who studies a martial art called Ving Tsun. This art is extremely popular in Hong Kong for various reasons that I won’t go into right now but if you’re curious you can ask me and I’ll be happy to answer. It was the practice of this martial art that introduced me to my husband, Matt Johnson who runs a kung fu school here in Chicago.
This martial art has a code of ethics that involves being a good citizen, being humble, promoting peace, and standing up for what is right and protecting those who need protection from bullies and so forth.
I made my first trip to Hong Kong a couple of years ago and I’ve been back a few times since then. Though I’m someone who likes spend a lot of time in remote locations being quiet and letting the busyness of my mind and heart settle down, I felt 100% in love with the city of Hong Kong, it’s culture, it’s people, and of course with my kung fu family there.
As a result it has been difficult watching the news and worrying about this place I love so much and the people who live there.
My concern for all of this led me to do a story for the Chicago Reader.
Here's a link to that: https://www.chicagoreader.com/chicago/photos-hong-kong-protest-freedom/Content?oid=73815391
I’m extremely grateful to the reader for giving me the time and space that it did. I made all the photographs, did all the interviews, and wrote all the text with guidance from the amazing Reader staff. In the process of working on that story I began to see, that much that was going on in Hong Kong seems to not quite be making it into the news. This made me want to go to Hong Kong and do more.
The stories we have been seeing her only the tip of the iceberg. I’m interested in the stories of ordinary people, their everyday life, and what they do.
How do they support each other in the midst of such extreme difficulty?
I want to understand the impact of what’s happening in this interaction between the Beijing mainland Chinese government in the city of Hong Kong in the Hong Kong people.
It’s interesting that Hong Kong has roots and connections stretching out from the city, all over the globe. While working on the story I’ve met many people here in Chicago who have a deep connections to Hong Kong.
I want to go and photograph an interview to help amplify the voices of those people not being heard as much as they might be.
Why do the events Hong Kong matter to you wherever you might live?
Number one. Hong Kong people are simply asking for fundamental human rights to be recognized.
Number two. The Hong Kong people are asking for the promises made by the Chinese government to be kept.
Number three. The Hong Kong people want their freedom.
All people everywhere around the world want their fundamental human rights, they want promises to be kept and they want freedom.
If we all look into our own hearts I believe we will see this truth is self evident.
What’s happening in Hong Kong matters to all of us, because all of us want the same things; freedom, respect- both given and received, dignity, and agency.
Further, for those of us living in other parts of the world, if we think that what’s happening in Hong Kong cannot happen to us wherever it is that we happen to live, I think if you forgive me, that view is naïve.
The road to tyranny is a slippery slope.
First one right is eroded, then another, then another.
For this trip to Hong Kong all the groundwork is in place.
Because of the network being built up over the years and as a result of my recent work, there are people on the ground in Hong Kong ready to help with making connections, translation, safety and getting around and so forth.
My intention is to get to Hong Kong do my work at the photographer and then do my best to get those stories out into the world so that everyone can know what is going on.
But I need help with the expenses.
Airfare and hotel around $2100-2400 depending on flight details
Transportation in Hong Kong When the MTR is shut down taxis may be necessary - estimating maybe $300
Money to pay translators and other fixtures and facilitators estimating $300-500
A laptop to process photos while I’m there so I can send them out to editors at various news outlets - around $200-300
I’m hoping to raise $3500. to cover all of that as well as some of my bills while I’m away so that the lights and heat are still on when I return home.
Addition I’ll provide links to news outlets as well as the story I did for the reader so that you can get more information about the situation over there.
I’ll also link or attach a video that I made about the story.
As things when I’m planning to offer in addition to publicly thinking everyone who supports this is the creation of a private Facebook group where I post updates photos and video from my time in Hong Kong.
This content will be exclusively for anyone who supports this trip.
I’m excited to announce that someone already made a first donation of $500 before even launched this campaign which let me adjust the amount needed to $3500
Honestly I wasn’t even planning on doing this but so many people said to me that they wanted to support the trip and believe in the mission of supporting truth and openness and democracy, that I pushed past my own discomfort and jumped in.
I want to thank all of you in advance for your support and help.
Please know that even if you can’t donate money to this trip, I’d be very grateful for your repeated sharing of the campaign. We all know how this works, and whether we like it or not it requires a certain diligence. A lather rinse and repeat process.
For those of you who can donate, please know how grateful I am for your support. And that no donation is too small or too large.
Again my heartfelt thanks. You should know also that I’ve never felt more sense of mission or purpose in going after story. This has my whole heart and I hope very much but I’ll find out that’s for publishing material of the world to know what is going on in Hong Kong at this critical time in history.
As a final note, I want to add that one of the things I’ve heard lately, is that China may be starting to crack down on the practice of martial arts.
This truly is history repeating itself. This happened during the period of conflict between the Ming and Qing dynasty.
It happened again during the cultural revolution.
And now it’s happening once again.
Why does China always clamp down on martial artists?
Because martial artists, as part of their training, learn how important it is to stand up and fight when it’s necessary. The core of traditional martial arts is about values that respect all people and offer protection to those who need it.
I like to think that with my camera I’m bringing the spirit of kung fu, of the Ving Tsun I love, to my practice using my camera to help protect and defend those in Hong Kong.
I hope that you’ll join me in this fight.
Let me know what questions you may have.
Happy to try my best to answer.
May all be safe, happy, strong and at ease. ❤️

content:
Fundraiser by Su Lee : Wipe Away Su Lee's Tears from her Composing Nights
Su Lee is organizing this fundraiser.
Dear friends, music lovers, and new music supporters,
It’s me, Su Lee, and I am currently working on my dissertation concert (for my Ph.D. in composition) which will be held on Sept. 9th 2019 Monday at 7:30pm in Lippes Concert Hall in Slee Hall at University at Buffalo.
The title of my dissertation composition and concert is Die Radikalen Tasten (The Radical Keys) in terms of aesthetics, Klang (sound), and theme.
I am writing a concerto for organ with keyboard ensemble, namely for our own tremendous Fisk Op.95 organ at UB. It will involve organ soloist with 1 assistant, 2 pianos (1 quarter-tone flat piano), 2 harpsichords (1 quarter-tone flat harpsichord), and 2 vibraphones which is a very rare instrumentation for microtonal new music.
The 1st half of the program features significant keyboard works from the 20th century such as Messiaen's solo organ work and Ives's quarter-tone piano pieces. As a special request from Dr. Fuller, who was in charge of the installation of the Fisk Op.95 organ at UB, I'm playing my very first organ transcription of Wagner's orchestral work.
The 2nd half of the program features my own 'radical' politically inspired compositions including a choral piece with organ accompaniment (dedicated to the UUCB Choir family) and my dissertation organ concerto. Both works are based on the Korean Democratic Uprising in May 1980 and the protest song written for the victims of the subsequent Gwangju massacre - a song that has became widely popular for activists and protesters, including those participating in the on-going Hong Kong protests.
Overall, it is a very colorful and unique combination and a rare program which is a you-don’t-want-to-miss concert.
I am modestly asking you for a little or big help in making my dissertation concert happen smoothly, especially given my financial struggles in not being able to even work legally for money off campus in America due to my visa status.
Your generous donation will be spent towards, (besides helping me wipe away all my tears and whining from composing numerous nights over the past few months and rehearsing in the upcoming days and nights):
Nine Musicians’ Performance Fee, about $3,000 – 3,300
Rent/Labor for Lippes Concert Hall in Slee Hall, about $1,000
Other concert related costs; buying performing materials, copying/binding score/parts, printing poster/program book, audio/video recording, photographing, tuning, reception, etc. about $1,200 – 1,500
Fortunately, I got awarded the MDRF (research fund) for $3,000 at UB so that I can be reimbursed afterwards, but I need money upfront now to pay first, and possibly more, to pay my dream team musicians fairly and to cover other costs.
Your genuine help means SO MUCH to me being an international Ph.D. student with many restrictions on earning money (3 months summer break without job, seriously!), as it will lighten my financial burdens and psychological anxiety when I absolutely need to focus more on my creative activities.
Simply speaking, you are contributing to a potentially "fabulous" new music piece, stimulating my further musical activities and making me believe that life (and the world) is so beautiful!
Every single one of your names will be acknowledged in my concert program book, and to thank you all, but not nearly enough, I like to give you in return as below:
$1~$49: a thank-you-card with a cover of a handwritten excerpt of my score
$50~$99: a thank-you-card like above AND a dvd of my dissertation concert (after my concert)
$100~$199: a thank-you-card AND a dvd like above, PLUS the autographed full score of my dissertation composition
$200~$299: EVERYTHING above AND one additional dvd of my Masters organ recitals (your choice of “Über den Namen B-A-C-H” or “Celebrating Lou Harrison’s 100th Birth-Year at Thunder Night”)
$300 or more: EVERYTHING above, PLUS a gift pack of Korean snacks/sweets/tea etc.
Please write me an email with your home address!
I am really excited to prepare my dissertation concert. Though I feel like this is sadly going to be my last self designed concert during my time in Buffalo (at UB), so I cannot wait to see many of you there!
Thank you so much for reading this and considering your donation.
I promise to pay you back with my "fabulous" new compositions and my performance, with the great help of my dream team of musician fellows!
Please feel free to spread the link to your social pages like Facebook, Instagram, or Twitter, or to emails, to help get the word out!
FYI, I am collecting your donations from now till October and GoFundMe takes 2.9% for transaction fee plus $0.30 PER Donation. Or you can donate by sending me a check to my place (email me for asking my address please!)

Fundraiser by Hong Kong Forum : 自由雕塑公園之『香港地』香港抗爭者雕像金屬牌匾 及 新壁畫
Hong Kong Forum for Hong Kong Forum Los Angeles
Hong Kong Forum for Hong Kong Forum Los Angeles
Hong Kong Forum is organizing this fundraiser to benefit Hong Kong Forum Los Angeles.
Hong Kong Forum for Hong Kong Forum Los Angeles
5年過去了，彷彿一切烽煙已經在時間中沈沒，然而有些人仍然選擇不去遺忘。
Five years have passed since Hong Konger's last attempt to maintain their freedom, and it seems that all dust has settled. However, some people still choose not to forget.
經過多方努力，我們在Yermo的自由雕塑公園（Liberty Sculpture Park）建立起了香港地，用藝術去銘記香港人的意志不滅。
After many efforts, we have established Hong Kong Corner in the Liberty Sculpture Park in Yermo, using art to remember the unyielding will of the Hong Kongers.
香港地的維護和創作需要長期的投入，我們亟需你的支持。不論捐款多少，都代表著你對香港所出的一分力。
The maintenance and creation of Yermo's "Hong Kong Corner" requires long-term investment, and we urgently need your support. Any donation, no matter the amount, represents your contribution to the undying spirit of Hong Kongers.
We hope to meet in a free Hong Kong someday.
Donation serves 3 main purposes.
1. 現時香港地有四件展品，沙漠氣候極端，冬寒夏焰，烈日風沙，我們要定期維修，提供防曬材料予連儂牆， 令他們可以日久維新。
1. Currently, Hong Kong Corner has four exhibits. We need to perform regular maintenance for some of the art works and provide sun & water protection sealants in the harsh desert weather condition.
2. 香港抗爭者的雕像現時沒有任何解釋。 在我們維修的過程當中，經常見到美國本地人到訪，但他們對於2019抗爭一事並不了清楚。希望可以籌款建立一塊金屬牌匾， 刻上中英文描述，令到到訪者了解究竟發生了什麼事。
2. The statues of Hong Kong Protesters currently have no explanations. During our maintenance work, we often see local Americans visiting, but they are not familiar with the 2019 protests. We hope to raise funds to establish a metal plaque with descriptions in both Chinese and English to help visitors understand what happened.
3. 自由雕塑公園的創辦人陳維明老師亦為香港地建立了新牆，我們希望可以籌款聘請來自香港的專業藝術家，以壁畫描繪出香港的景況。
3. Mr. Chen Wei Ming, the art creator of Liberty Sculpture Park, has also built a new wall for Hong Kong Land. We hope to raise funds to pay for the expenses of hiring a professional artist from Hong Kong to depict the situation in Hong Kong with a mural.

content:
Fundraiser by tyrone thomas : Unite for Digital Fearlessness
tyrone thomas is organizing this fundraiser.
"Use what's in your hand" - Adam Clayton Powell Jr.
Your phone isn't just for posting stories and playing music. That little computer in your pocket has more power than entire governments had 20 years ago. Like the ancient Abhaya Mudra - the fearless hand gesture that banishes fear and offers protection from the "Evil Eye" - we're transforming these devices into something that helps communities meet the coming challenges with a sense of fearlessness, rooted in Free Collaboration and Privacy.
Abhaya started as disaster recovery - how do communities rebuild communication when the towers are down and the power's out? But we realized something profound: the same tools that help neighborhoods coordinate after a hurricane are exactly what we need when authoritarians try to silence us. Like the protective Abhaya Mudra, this system creates a shield against the "evil eye" of surveillance while becoming a helpful digital companion that guides and empowers our communities.
Drawing inspiration from Buckminster Fuller's vision of global cooperation for humanity's benefit, Abhaya is designed as the foundation for communities to work together toward a more equitable future. The ecosystem operates through five interconnected elements:
• Tor + Mobile based Mesh Networks: Messages that flow around censorship like water
• Mesh Based Distributed Storage: Truth that lives everywhere so it can't be destroyed
• Mesh Based Distributed Computation Service: AI-capable shared processing power for communities to solve their own challenges
• Sensor/Peripheral IO: User Controlled Eyes and ears embedded in the network
• Mesh Federation: Connecting local networks into unstoppable global resistance
"The ultimate measure of a man is not where he stands in moments of comfort and convenience, but where he stands at times of challenge and controversy." - MLK Jr.
After Hurricane Katrina, communities learned they couldn't wait for official help. Hong Kong protesters used mesh networks when the government tried to cut them off. Iranian women shared videos of police brutality when the state blocked social media. Puerto Ricans coordinated mutual aid through amateur radio when Maria destroyed the grid.
The pattern is clear: when systems fail - whether from natural disasters or deliberate suppression - communities need tools to build their own infrastructure. Communities united in purpose and vision can be powerful.
When you contribute to Abhaya, you're investing in infrastructure that makes communities fearless. No CEO can sell it. No government can buy it. No algorithm can suppress it. No storm can wash it away.
Every dollar helps us turn individual devices into collective power. Like Powell said - we're not waiting for someone to save us. We're using what's already in our hands to build the infrastructure of fearlessness.
Fund the network that makes communities fearless.
We're assembling an international team of developers and engineers who understand that code is power, and power should belong to the people. If you're a technologist looking to put your skills toward meaningful resistance, this is how you push back against authoritarianism and corporate overreach.
• Onion Router, I2P, Freenet protocols
• DevOps/SecOps fluent in Dark Web technologies
This is open-source work with no revenue model - Abhaya is designed to be free for all communities. For technologists feeling the weight of current events, it's a concrete way to turn skills into direct action and fulfill civic duty through code. Ready to put your shoulder to the wheel of progress? Reach out.
Because true community care means building the infrastructure that makes us all fearless.

content:
Fundraiser by The Lantos Foundation : Legal Defense for Hong Kong Democracy Activists
The Lantos Foundation for Tom Lantos Foundation for Human Rights & Justice
The Lantos Foundation for Tom Lantos Foundation for Human Rights & Justice
The Lantos Foundation is organizing this fundraiser to benefit Tom Lantos Foundation for Human Rights & Justice.
The Lantos Foundation for Tom Lantos Foundation for Human Rights & Justice
The Lantos Foundation for Human Rights & Justice stands with the people of Hong Kong on the front lines of the fight for freedom & democracy.
Courageous Hong Kong democracy activists have been protesting for months against a dangerous Chinese extradition bill that would have undermined their independence and freedom. Though the bill has now been formally withdrawn, the fight is not over. Since June, thousands of protesters have been attacked and injured by police and mainland gangs and over 1,100 people have been detained. Those arrested for peacefully protesting have been charged with offenses that could put them in jail for many years.
Hong Kong Democracy protesters have won the first huge victory in the court of public opinion, but the next victories will need to be won in the courts of law.
Just a few months ago, the Lantos Foundation was proud to give our highest award to the most recognizable leader of the democracy movement – Joshua Wong. While such leadership is important, all of the brave democracy crusaders deserve more than our admiration. We must equip them to defend themselves against the crushing apparatus of the Chinese communist state. This legal defense fund aims to support Joshua and his compatriots as they defend themselves against false accusations that could land them in prison for years to come.
Our hope is that we can match their courage and determination in the form of financial support that will ensure they have fair representation. It is critical that the rule of law be upheld at this pivotal moment in Hong Kong's history. The eyes of the world may be on Hong Kong, but the eyes of history will be on those of us enjoying our own freedom and democracy - let us match our words and good wishes with the resources to defend those on the front lines of this fight for freedom.
These legal defense funds will be officially disbursed through the Lantos Foundation's Front Line Fund grant program.

在中国电动汽车行业，供应商一直在默默承受着苦难。经济观察报今年9月对14家汽车制造商的财务数据进行了调查，发现其平均应付账款和应付票据周转期从2025年底的164.4天上升到2026年上半年的187.5天。这意味着汽车制造商向供应商付款的时间更长，供应商需要资金支付工人工资和购买生产投入。这可能会导致许多供应商借钱来支付日常费用。
继去年 17 家主要汽车制造商承诺将供应商付款期限限制为 60 天后，北京于 2026 年 9 月出台了新规则来管理汽车制造商向供应商付款的方式。这可能有效；据中国汽车工业协会统计，平均付款周期为54天，比去年同期缩短约10天。
这看似与经济观察报的调查结果相矛盾，但应该指出的是，他们使用了两种不同的衡量标准。行业协会衡量从接受发票到付款（包括某些银行票据付款）的时间，而期刊使用的财务报表衡量标准则使用应付账款，包括承兑汇票和销售成本。它可能会夸大付款期限，因为它包括承兑汇票，但不包括未售出产品的成本。然而，它确实指出了这样一个事实：供应商可能会收到金融工具而不是现金，而检查或发票处理的延迟可能会进一步延长等待时间。
供应商付款问题不仅限于汽车行业。正如中国人民银行金融市场司司长曹媛媛在 9 月 14 日的政府吹风会上承认的那样，拥有大量现金储备的大公司推迟了向供应商付款，迫使规模较小的供应商借款以继续运营。这代表融资成本从较大企业向较小企业的转移。
这突显了中国制造业经常受到关注的不平等现象。大公司可以通过提高效率来减少对营运资金的需求，但也可以通过延长向供应商付款的时间，将财务负担转移到供应链上。在某些情况下，大公司会发出稍后付款的数字承诺，供应商将其提交给银行以获得贷款。这种做法有时会被那些希望推迟现金付款同时向供应商收取融资费用的公司滥用。
据统计，这些未偿还的凭证在高峰时期达到了3万亿元人民币，但到2026年7月已降至2.4万亿元人民币。

In China’s electric vehicle industry, suppliers have been silently suffering. An investigation by Economic Observer carried out in September of this year examined financial data from 14 automakers, finding that their average accounts-payable and notes-payable turnover period had risen from 164.4 days at the end of 2025 to 187.5 days in the first half of 2026. This means that automakers have been taking longer to pay their suppliers, who need the funds to pay workers and purchase production inputs. This may cause many suppliers to borrow money to cover their everyday costs.
After 17 major vehicle manufacturers promised to limit supplier payment periods to 60 days last year, Beijing introduced new rules in September 2026 to govern how automakers pay their suppliers. This may be working; according to the China Association of Automobile Manufacturers, the average payment period was 54, about 10 days shorter than a year earlier.
This does seemingly contradict the findings of the Economic Observer, but it should be pointed out that they use two different measures. The industry association measured time from acceptance of an invoice until payment, including payment by certain bank bills, while the financial statement measure used by the journal uses accounts payable, including acceptance bills, and cost of goods sold. It may overstate payment periods because it includes acceptance bills while excluding the cost of unsold products. However, it does point to the fact that suppliers may receive a financial instrument instead of cash, while delays in inspection or invoice processing can further extend the wait.
The supplier payment issue is not limited to the automotive sector. As Cao Yuanyuan, director general of the People’s Bank of China’s Financial Market Department, acknowledged in a September 14 government briefing, large companies with substantial cash reserve have delayed supplier payments, forcing smaller suppliers to borrow to continue operating. This represents a transfer of financing costs from larger to smaller firms.
This highlights an inequality that often goes under the radar in China’s manufacturing sector. Large firms can reduce their need for working capital by becoming more efficient, but also by taking longer to pay their suppliers, moving the financial burden up the supply chain. In some cases, large companies have issued a digital promise to pay later, which the supplier presents to a bank to obtain a loan. This practice has sometimes been abused by companies looking to postpone cash payments while charging suppliers financing fees.
These outstanding certificates reached 3 trillion yuan at their peak, but had fallen to 2.4 trillion yuan by July 2026, according to the central bank. Average payment periods for the certificates had fallen to 92 days, which demonstrates progress but considerable scale of such arrangements.
For context, at the end of September 2026, large industrial firms held 29.77 trillion yuan in accounts receivable, a year-on-year increase of 10 percent. Their average collection period was about 72 days. This illustrates how much working capital is tied up in unpaid invoices in China’s manufacturing industry.
Why does this matter? True, longer payment periods require suppliers to borrow and pay financing costs, but suppliers also may have to postpone growth and innovation. Suppliers may also be forced to accept less favorable contract terms to keep large customers. This is detrimental to industries that rely on smaller manufacturers in particular, since postponing supplier payments reduces the capabilities of the supplier pool.
However, it seems that Chinese officials recognize these risks. According to the September automotive regulations, most production materials must be inspected within three working days and automakers may not force suppliers to accept certain noncash payment instruments. They also encourage firms to pay smaller suppliers within 30 to 60 days. A State Council directive called for even broader reforms, including tighter oversight of electronic certificates and greater scrutiny of large companies with substantial payables.
Despite this, enforcement of these measures remains challenging, as firms in highly competitive industries may attempt other ways to lower their costs, such as negotiating lower prices from their suppliers. These actions would also constrain suppliers’ financial health and innovation.
For international businesses looking to source from China, these cash flow issues may reduce supplier flexibility, which can prevent the overseas firm from responding to growing demand. A supplier may have the capabilities required by a large multinational, but a lack of cash may prohibit them from investing in improvements or expanding capacity to meet international market demand. Buying firms therefore need to assess the financial health of their suppliers, not just their existing capacity and delivery performance.
China’s competitive place in global manufacturing disguises a tension beneath the surface: large manufacturers may gain market share but potentially at the expense of the very suppliers that keep them in business. Whether Beijing can ensure supplier protection while preserving the competitiveness of large manufacturers will test the policymaking skills of China’s technocrats.

content:
资料照片：驻立陶宛台湾代表处摆放的台湾与立陶宛旗帜。(2022年1月20日)
台湾外交部星期二(11月10日)对有媒体报道称，立陶宛外交部曾在9月要台湾驻立陶宛代表处更名一事不予评论。台湾外交部次长陈明祺说，目前没有更名计划。不过有立陶宛议会外委会成员称，该国外交部官员要求台湾代表处更名的行为或涉违法，要求召开特别会议展开调查。
立陶宛网络媒体Delfi星期一报导，立陶宛外交部副部长维德曼塔斯·韦尔比茨卡斯(Vidmantas Verbickas)曾在9月24日递交一份非正式文件给台湾驻立陶宛代表王雪虹，要求驻立陶宛台湾代表处在一个星期内更名。
报道说，该份文件称，驻立陶宛台湾代表处现行名称阻碍该国与台湾关系发展，要求台湾代表处在10月1日前更名；作为交换，立陶宛将提供台湾签署双边投资前景协议的机会，并启动避免双重课税及贸易协议谈判。此外，该文件也设想了在外交部内设立台湾事务特使一职的可能性。
Delfi另一篇报道说，在有关立陶宛外交部敦促台湾更改代表处名称一事被报道后，立陶宛议会外交事务委员会副主席、保守派议员齐吉曼塔斯·帕维奥尼斯(Zygimantas Pavilionis)要求召开委员会特别会议，以审查外交部长凯斯图蒂斯·布德里斯(Kestutis Budrys)的作为。
“今天，我将请求所有外交事务委员会成员召开一个特别会议来讨论部长的行动——我认为这个行动是违法的，”帕维奥尼斯星期一在其脸书上贴文中写道。
台湾外交部次长陈明祺星期一到立法院备询前接受媒体联访时针对立陶宛媒体关于台湾代表处更名一事的报道表示，他对外界传闻没有任何评论，“尤其是基于假消息的一些推论”，有伤台立双方的互动及双边关系。
“当初这个名称也是双方基于要深化双边关系之后，才做的这样一个决定，”陈明祺说，“我方目前没有任何打算要更动我国驻立陶宛代表处的名称。”
与此同时，立陶宛国家广播电视网(LRT)星期一报道，中国外交官预计11月11至12日访问立陶宛，与外交部官员和一些“寻求与北京恢复外交关系的议会成员会面”，议员伊格纳斯·韦盖莱(Ignas Vegele)上星期五宣布了此一计划中的访问。
报道提到今年6月才成为立陶宛总理的明道加斯·辛克维丘斯(Mindaugas Sinkevicius)曾表明，他希望年底前能在与中国的谈判中取得突破，“恢复大使级外交代表关系已被纳入其政府的施政项目中。”
根据报道，立陶宛外交部长凯斯图蒂斯·布德里斯星期一对媒体关于外交部要求台湾代表处改名一事的报道回应说：“我不会评论这个信息。首先，它被错误报道。我们与不同互动伙伴有各种讨论，我当然不会去谈细节。”
他说：“我可以证实的是，我们与台湾方面谈到双边关系的各种层面。”
报道说，立陶宛总理明道加斯·辛克维丘斯的发言人盖达斯·萨利加(Gedas Saylyga)星期一也告诉媒体，“正如政府纲领的规划，外交部的目标是将与中国的外交关系恢复到与其他欧盟国家相同的水平。总理想看到的是最后的结果，而不是对过程发表评论。”
“行动计划的选择是外交部长的责任。立陶宛旨在与台湾保持互利的经济与务实的合作，”萨利加补充道。
中国外交部发言人郭嘉昆6月曾对中国与立陶宛的关系表示，当前中立关系的困难和症结在于立方违反一个中国原则，背弃了立方在两国建交公报中的政治承诺。“中方同立方沟通的大门始终敞开”，希望立方尽早采取行动，“果断纠正错误”，回到一个中国原则的正确轨道上来，为中立关系正常化创造条件。
台湾政府2021年在维尔纽斯设立“驻立陶宛台湾代表处”，这是台湾在欧洲第一个以“台湾”，而非“台北”为名所设的代表处，立国为此面对有正式外交关系的北京当局强大压力，中国以召回大使作为抗议，将关系单方面降至“代办”级别，并对立陶宛施加经济报复。
台湾外交部发言人萧光伟星期二在台北的例行记者会上，针对媒体关于立陶宛以非正式文件要台湾代表处改名一事的提问表示，外交部对报道所称的文件及相关臆测不予评论。
他说，驻立陶宛台湾代表处的名称“是台立两国政府基于共享的普世价值，坚信民主、维护自由，以及共同深化双边关系的意愿，经审慎协商达成的共识。”
萧光伟指出，立陶宛总统吉塔纳斯·瑙塞达(Gitanas Nausėda)曾在今年10月27日表示，立陶宛推动与中国关系正常化“不应与台湾代表处名称直接挂钩”，此外，立陶宛总理明道加斯·辛克维丘斯也曾表示，有机会在不更改代表处名称的情况下改善与中国的关系。
萧光伟强调，自台湾与立陶宛互设代表处以来，台湾政府持续与该国历任政府推动经贸投资、科技产业、教育文化与人道援助等领域的实质合作，双方并共同投入资源持续推动援助乌克兰及重建合作计划，以具体行动支持乌克兰，实践民主前线国家面对威权国家扩张、捍卫民主自由价值的共同承诺。
台湾外交部呼吁民主伙伴坚守共同理念与原则，相互支持，携手因应威权国家的胁迫与挑战，台湾愿意与立陶宛在诚信、尊重、互助及互惠的基础上持续深化双边关系。
